author: KevineCove
body:
Keep playing summoner and pick up the Buggane summon the next time the event is in season. Switch to Beowulf at 225 and from there start slowly farming whatever endgame build you want. At a certain point your endgame build will be stronger than your Beo (unless Beo is your endgame) and you can fully switch over.

To level up, keep trying to find kingdoms until you get one where you can farm Dracon. Dracon gives the most XP relative to the orns it costs the kingdom to host, so just hammer him over and over and you'll level up really fast. Other raids too if your kingdom is okay with the orn expenditure. Having a friend carry you through boss horde raids while you have XP buffs will level you quickly, so will hitting world bosses from a bus or train. Getting carried through world raid bosses by high level players is another very fast way to level up, if you have some summoning scrolls it should be easy to find someone that will run your raids with you.

Towers move every week, so don't worry about the best location. Get some gear that boosts your view distance, mine is close to 1km and significantly more with buffs, very few areas are truly in the middle of nowhere.

Move your origin town to where you are. The only real reason to move it is to be able to open your WayVessel which you can only do by physically being there, but social play is by far the best way to power level and reach endgame.

author: dreambig5
body:
Welcome back!

1. I think u/KevineCove covered alot of it. 

This here is probably what can help you the most: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aA4za2mOqvx1AosEIf9JmztPSTr5wh5wmfiaraL\_YYw/edit?tab=t.0](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aA4za2mOqvx1AosEIf9JmztPSTr5wh5wmfiaraL_YYw/edit?tab=t.0)

This is probably the best compilation of resources (Class guides (including new best builds), hidden info, tips & almost everything you need). 

I've found this site quite helpful as well: [https://codex.fqegg.top/#/](https://codex.fqegg.top/#/) (in the link above, it mentions [orna.guide](http://orna.guide) site but it no longer seems to be up & running so this is my preferred source for codexing, determining quality, comaring gear, and checking on tower schedules).

Theree are also plenty of other videos on Youtube which can help you out but I'm not sure if there are many that are staying up to date or providing as clear explanations as Shabbash. 

Lastly, I just found out about this site: [https://playerecho.com/orna/](https://playerecho.com/orna/) but I've not gone over all the material yet.  

2.  The best way to deal with this is working on maxing out your VD (Viewing Distance). This requires multiple steps:

* There are probably a lot more dungeons in your area but you just can't see them. If you go to your status page, you can see what your current VD is. The max is 1600 meters (1.6 km which is almost 1 Mile).
* Accessories: I don't know how far you got in the main questline. I remember taking time off from the game and by the time I came back, I basically was able to do the main questline again (if you're able to, do it! this can get you 2 unfelled concords). An unfelled concord is one of my most favorite accessories because it gives you: +20% viewing distance, +50% luck bonus & Dungeon Cooldown: -50%. Have 2 is amazing but sometimes I mix it up (one unfelled concord & a mighty lantern to get the same viewing distance bonus but to give myself more time to go through the dungeons/monuments). Rather than being stuck waiting waiting for 6 hours for the cooldown, you are able to enter dungeons/monuments quicker.
* Weapon slots: you want to pick up helhests & surtr swords (there is a Tier 5 version of it and also T10 version). You can get the T5 one until you hit T10. I'd suggest getting both the sword and helhests but only upgrade & adorn the T10 ones. The T10 Surtr sword once maxed out (godforged) has 8 adornment slots & they can be dual weilded using any class. The T10 Helhest bows (godforged) have 9 adornment slots each.
   * The adornment: Kill as many Third Horseman raids for the adornment called Symbol of War (which gives +2% additional viewing distance each). I'd try to get 34 atleast.
* Class: Dedicate a special class for VD. I suggest doing this on the Magistrate class (it can use weapons/gear for any class), and give it the specialization "Seeker" which specifically gives you more VD.
* Amity: I'm not sure if you're new to memory hunts like I was when I came back to the game. Lmk if you need help with this. You want to do memory hunts to find the best VD Amity that you can (I believe +5% is the max one). Btw Memory hunts are a great way to get ton of orns, exp & gold easily (but that requires a seperate build).
* Head slot: The best gear in the head slot for VD are: Argos/Corvyn's Porcelain Mask (+20% VD), Fallen Sky Hood (+10% VD bonus)
* NEW! The Travelers Guild has also changed. If you go to the bottom right corner & click on the footsteps icon, you'll see there are now bonuses for # of steps (broken down into 3 tiers). If you click on the ? next to earn bonus level it'll show you that you can get bonuses to +10% bonus to VD at tiers 1 and 2 (as well as XP, Orns, Luck, & Memory interaction range which is for Memory Hunts/Amities). These last 12 hours each. 

The rest of these basically give you a VD bonus for 1 hour each. 

* Consumables: Torches are cheap & give you some VD, Farsight is a potion that you can make/consume (I recommend stacking up on both of these). 
* Be sure to light your brazier once a day from your Keep/Fortress/Castle or through an outpost. Go to Lookout -> Light Brazier.
* NEW! The Spelunking gameplay has changed & it's more like dungeons. Whenever you complete dungeons or mystic caves, goblin fortresses, etc. You'll pick up proofs of Spelunking. You can go to your Spelunking Guild in your hometown, go to the section which says Torches and buy various torches to make the most of your dungeon runs. All of them give +20% bonus each.

The gameplay sped up QUITE a bit for me once I figured out the importance of building for VD. You'll also be able to find tons of inns around you (so you can pick up lot more quests which you can complete for easy xp/orns/gold). **I used to think I only had 1-2 dungeons around me but I realized I have usually atleast 13-15 dungeons around me, random number of monuments, several towers (other than what I've built as well).**

    I want to clarify that you don't need to do ALL of the above to reach the max viewing distance of 1600 meters.  

3. If you're enjoying summoner class yes ofcourse. But I'd also make sure to have Beowulf as backup as previously suggested by kevinecove. It'll help you with completing raids quicker (given that you pick up those followers), also being able to complete towers (some hordes, are hard to survive with just summoner in early T10), and also to be the final tower raid boss. Aside from the followers mentions, here are my favorite summons for T10:

* Cockatrice: Plain & simple. If you're struggling with raids or Prometheus Tower boss, you want to make sure they're petrified so you can just chip away at them without worrying about taking damage. One of the best starting summons along with Phaeton.
* Ancient Jinn: Used to be the best AoE summon that you get when you are using the Benefactor Specialization (which you can start using at T9)
* Peluda, the Poisoned one (T19 dragon summon from Wyrmhunt event). Does amazing AoE damage. I love running this with Ancient Dragon (Ancient dragon applies Drakeblight which makes that target weak to Dragon attacks, and Peluda's Quillstorm skill which is a multiple dragon-based attack to all opponents/horde).
* Ancient Dragon: It is a T10 summon that you get once you purchase Grand Summoner Hydrus (celestial class) from Tower Guild (aka Titan Workshop) and reach lvl 230.  It's a tank & can inflict Drakeblight as mentioned above.
* Phaeton: T10 summon that you get once you purchase Grand Summoner Auriga (celestial class) from Tower Guild (aka Titan Workshop) and reach lvl 230. It gives you or your summons random bonuses (including itself). 
* Arisen Spiritgarm: During Ragnarok event, you want to defeat the T10 Jormundurr Raid to pick up an **Arisen Spiritgarm Grimoire** (which you'll need to equip to your shield/offhand slot). These summons hit hard but take some time to charge up (First they usually use Great meditation skill which takes 2 turns but temporarily boosts magical damage greatly) and then they start preparing to cast a magical attack which takes 3 turns but can do considerable amount of damage. \*Honestly, I used to love using this but I realized you can do more damage quicker by using Beo class with the Arisen Spiritgarm follower.
* Very Scary Skeleton (which you already have): I like to summon this last but having atleast one is good for the temporary debuffs it provides.
* Chimera: T10. Does decent damage and is quick to summon. Available when  you unlock Grand Summoner class (reach lvl 225). 

The summons I've mentioned are really good when using Grand Summoner Auriga class, with benefactor spec. I don't play Grand Summoner Hydrus as much so check the doc I linked above & go to the Grand Summoner classline guide. 

4. This is just my opinion but kingdoms ....meh. It's hard to rely on others so I've just run my own solo kingdom for my main character & alts. My kingdom is almost lvl 50. I don't care about gauntlets (used to be really important in early gameplay when the game came out in order to get the kingdom to lvl 20 to have access to all the kingdom raids). I lvled up just by doing the kingdom quests using my main & alts. I have full control over the kingdom orns, & florens. 

Honestly, just getting on in game chat or discord & partying up with someone temporarily to do raids or dungeons together is enough to gain plenty of exp. 

But if you want to go down the kingdom route, use the discord channel (community links).

5. Move your origin town to where you are. If you want to set up wayvessels (learn about using alts). I've created plenty of alts to be able to set up wayvessels at multiple locations (some for fishing, some for beastiaries, some for access to dungeons, and some just so I can have a place to summon raids).
